content.title: About
content.content: Portabella mushroom (Portabella) is a large, fully mature specimen of the common button mushroom (Agaricus bisporus). It features a thick, brown cap up to 15 cm in diameter, a meaty texture, a subtle nutty aroma and a mildly sweet flavor. Portabellas are frequently used as a meat substitute in vegetarian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Portabella is simply a fully grown button mushroom; its size and color change as it matures.
The mushroom contains vitamin D2, which is produced when exposed to ultraviolet light.
In Japan, portabellas are often marinated in soy sauce and used in sushi rolls.
It can absorb up to 20 % of its weight in marinades, making it an excellent flavor carrier.
Storing portabellas in a paper bag rather than plastic helps prevent excess moisture.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Portabellas provide niacin (B3), riboflavin (B2) and pyridoxine (B6), which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: A 100 g serving contains about 3 g of protein with only 22 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly option.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Selenium and polyphenols in the mushroom help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Beta‑glucans in the cell walls stimulate activity of immune cells.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms, ranging from skin rashes to respiratory issues.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Mushrooms are relatively high in purines, so people with gout should limit intake.

items.title: Risk of mycotoxins
items.content: Improperly stored mushrooms can develop toxins; always purchase fresh, intact specimens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Portabellas can be grilled, roasted, sautéed, or stewed. The cap is often used as a "steak," while the stem works well in sauces. They pair nicely with olive oil, garlic, herbs, and balsamic vinegar. Before cooking, gently wipe the cap with a damp cloth to remove dirt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store portabellas in the refrigerator in a paper bag or a container with ventilation to avoid excess moisture. They stay fresh for 3–5 days when kept properly. For longer storage, blanch for 2–3 minutes and freeze.
